name: Individual tax returns
fee_basis: Fixed fee, quoted before we start
turnaround: About 3 weeks from a complete organizer
summary: Federal and state returns for individuals and families, reviewed by a partner, with a short letter explaining what changed from last year.
body: Every return is prepared by one person and reviewed by another. With the finished return you get a one-page letter: what you owe or get back, what changed from last year, and what to set aside for next year's estimates.
includes: Federal and state returns|E-filing and e-signature|Comparison with last year|Estimate vouchers for next year|Answers to questions all year
bring: Last year's return (new clients)|W-2s, 1099s and K-1s|Mortgage interest and property tax statements|Charitable receipts over $250|Childcare and education costs|Records of estimated payments made

name: Business tax returns
fee_basis: Fixed fee by entity and complexity
turnaround: Before the March or April due date, or extended
summary: Returns for S corporations, partnerships, C corporations and single-member LLCs, with owners' K-1s delivered early.
body: We prepare the business return from books we keep or from yours, and deliver owners' K-1s early enough for their personal returns. If the books need work first, we quote the cleanup separately.
includes: Federal and state business returns|K-1s for every owner|Depreciation schedules|State franchise and annual reports|A review meeting with a partner
bring: Year-end trial balance or access to your books|Bank and loan statements for December|Fixed asset purchases and sales|Payroll year-end reports|Owner distributions and contributions

name: Monthly bookkeeping and close
summary: Reconciled books every month, closed on the fifth business day, with a one-page summary and a list of open questions.
body: We reconcile every bank, card and loan account each month, post payroll and adjusting entries, and close the books on the fifth business day. You get a profit and loss, a balance sheet and a one-page note with anything that needs your answer.
includes: Bank, card and loan reconciliations|Monthly profit and loss and balance sheet|One-page monthly summary|Sales tax filings|Year-end package for the tax return
bring: Read-only access to bank and card feeds|Receipts for purchases over $75|Loan statements|Notes on unusual deposits

name: Payroll and 1099s
summary: Payroll on your schedule, quarterly payroll returns, W-2s and 1099s, and setup for first-time employers.
body: We run payroll weekly, every two weeks or twice a month, file the quarterly and annual payroll returns, and send W-2s and 1099s by January 31. For first-time employers we register with the state and set up withholding accounts.
includes: Payroll runs and direct deposit|Quarterly payroll returns|State unemployment filings|W-2s and 1099-NECs in January|New-hire reporting
bring: Employee W-4s and state forms|Pay rates and schedules|Contractor W-9s|State employer account numbers

name: Tax planning and estimates
turnaround: Quarterly, two weeks before each estimate
summary: Four short check-ins a year so the estimates are right and there is no surprise in April.
body: Two weeks before each estimated payment we look at the year so far and set the amount. In November we meet for year-end planning: retirement contributions, the timing of large purchases and sales, and charitable giving.
includes: Quarterly estimate calculations|A November year-end planning meeting|Projections for big events: a sale, a move, retirement|Coordination with your financial adviser
bring: Pay stubs or business profit and loss to date|Investment statements|Notes on expected changes this year

name: Nonprofit 990s and audit-ready books
fee_basis: Fixed fee by revenue and complexity
turnaround: By May 15, or extended to November 15
summary: Form 990 or 990-EZ, books kept ready for the annual audit, and restricted fund tracking a volunteer treasurer can keep up.
body: We prepare the annual return and the state charity filing, keep restricted and unrestricted funds apart, and prepare the schedules your auditor asks for. Board treasurers get a quarterly report written for people who are not accountants.
includes: Form 990 or 990-EZ and state filing|Restricted fund tracking|Audit preparation schedules|Quarterly board treasurer report|Grant budget-to-actual reports
bring: Board minutes for the year|Grant agreements|Donor restrictions|Bank statements and payroll reports

name: IRS and state notice response
fee_basis: Per notice, quoted after we read it
turnaround: Reply within 10 business days of receiving it
summary: Send us the letter. An enrolled agent reads it, writes the reply, and tracks it until the agency closes it.
body: Most notices are about a form the agency has that the return did not show, or a payment applied to the wrong year. We match it, write the reply, and follow up until it is closed. For balances that cannot be paid at once, we set up a payment plan.
includes: Reading the notice and the return|A written reply and supporting documents|Tracking until the agency closes it|Payment plan setup if needed|Power of attorney filing
bring: A copy of the notice (all pages)|The return it refers to|Any payment confirmations

name: Estates and trusts
fee_basis: Fixed fee, quoted after the first meeting
summary: Fiduciary returns for estates and trusts, final individual returns, and the paperwork for executors and trustees.
body: We prepare the final individual return, the estate or trust return and beneficiaries' K-1s, and give executors a plain list of what is due and when.
includes: Final individual return|Estate or trust return (Form 1041)|Beneficiary K-1s|A filing calendar for the executor
bring: The will or trust document|Date-of-death account statements|Executor or trustee contact details
